data.name: Dinosaurs A Prehistoric Adventure
data.detailed_description:
Be the Dinosaur!

Experience the world of dinosaurs like never before! Dinosaurs A Prehistoric Adventure is an ARPG where you could play as 15 dinosaurs in a semi-open world environment.

Description

Dinosaurs A Prehistoric Adventure is an ARPG where you could play as 15 dinosaurs set in a fictional world. Even though the setting of this game is completely fictional, the dinosaurs included are modeled based on real world findings. Each dinosaur is unique and have their own strengths and weaknesses. This means that each dinosaur have their own way of overcoming challenges. Dinosaurs A Prehistoric Adventure includes two main modes, the adventure mode, where players would be able to play as a dinosaur, and an exhibition mode where players would get to know more about the dinosaurs.

Lore

The world of Dinosaurs A Prehistoric Adventure brings players to a post-apocalyptic prehistoric world where pods have erupted and released poisonous material to the atmosphere. The rapid increase of poisonous material in the air transform some of the inhabitants into mutated violent beings that are wreaking havoc in the land. These beings are guarding the source of the corruption and should be stop at all cost before more fell victim to this contamination.

Features

  • Play as 15 dinosaurs with each having their own strengths and weaknesses
  • ARPG elements combined with survival elements such as hunger, thirst, and much more
  • Rich and unique environments that are both challenging and fun to explore
  • Two game modes: Adventure Mode and Exhibition Mode
  • Simple controls

reviews.review:
Dinosaurs A Prehistoric Adventure is an ambitious yet imperfect indie action RPG that offers an interesting twist on prehistoric survival by placing players directly in control of dinosaurs. Developed and published by Arcupion Art, this free-to-play experience combines exploration, combat, and survival mechanics within a fictional world devastated by mysterious environmental contamination. Rather than following the traditional formula of hunting dinosaurs as a human protagonist, the game allows players to become these prehistoric creatures and experience their struggles firsthand. Its unusual premise provides an appealing foundation, particularly for dinosaur enthusiasts, although several limitations prevent the gameplay from reaching its full potential.

The story takes place in an alternate prehistoric environment where mysterious pods have released poisonous substances into the atmosphere, transforming ordinary wildlife into violent, mutated creatures. These dangerous beings threaten the surrounding ecosystem while guarding the sources responsible for spreading the contamination. Players must navigate this increasingly hostile landscape and confront the corrupted inhabitants to prevent further destruction. The combination of prehistoric animals and post-apocalyptic fantasy creates an intriguing setting that separates the game from conventional dinosaur simulators. However, the narrative remains relatively straightforward, serving primarily as background motivation rather than delivering an elaborate story filled with memorable characters or dramatic developments.

One of the game's most appealing features is its roster of 15 playable dinosaurs, each possessing different strengths and weaknesses. This variety encourages experimentation because individual creatures are intended to approach challenges differently. The dinosaurs are modeled with inspiration from actual paleontological discoveries, providing a recognizable connection to prehistoric history despite the fictional storyline. Controlling different species adds novelty to the experience and creates opportunities for players to discover their preferred survival strategies. Unfortunately, the mechanical differences do not necessarily translate into the depth expected from more sophisticated RPGs. While the selection is impressive for a modest independent production, the gameplay would benefit from more distinctive abilities, animations, and interactions.

Survival mechanics introduce additional responsibilities beyond simply defeating enemies. Players must account for hunger, thirst, and other environmental pressures while exploring the semi-open world. These systems are intended to create tension by making survival an ongoing concern rather than an automatic outcome. Managing basic necessities can provide a satisfying sense of progression when combined with exploration and combat. Nevertheless, the survival elements appear comparatively simple, and their repetitive nature may become noticeable during extended sessions. Players accustomed to elaborate crafting systems, detailed ecological simulations, or complex resource management should recognize that this title offers a considerably more streamlined interpretation of the genre.

Combat is another significant component, particularly when confronting the mutated creatures responsible for spreading corruption. The ability to select dinosaurs with different characteristics provides some strategic possibilities, encouraging players to consider the advantages and disadvantages of their chosen species. The accessible control scheme makes the basic gameplay relatively approachable, although simplicity also limits the complexity of encounters. Combat lacks the refinement and tactical sophistication that would make repeated confrontations consistently exciting. Enemy encounters and character interactions could benefit from more responsive mechanics and greater variety. Consequently, the action works best as a casual diversion rather than a demanding combat experience.

The semi-open-world environments provide opportunities to wander through prehistoric landscapes while searching for challenges and surviving environmental threats. The combination of natural scenery and fictional corruption gives the setting a distinctive atmosphere. However, the world does not consistently deliver the environmental complexity or interactive depth that its concept suggests. Exploration can become less rewarding when locations offer limited activities beyond movement, survival maintenance, and combat. Visually, the game demonstrates the modest production values associated with smaller independent projects. Its presentation is functional rather than spectacular, with dinosaur models and environments providing the necessary foundation without achieving the realism or animation quality found in more technically advanced titles.

A particularly welcome feature is the inclusion of two separate gameplay modes. Adventure Mode focuses on controlling dinosaurs, exploring environments, and confronting dangers, while Exhibition Mode offers information about the prehistoric creatures represented in the game. This educational addition provides value for players interested in learning about dinosaurs rather than exclusively engaging in action-oriented gameplay. Although the exhibition content should not be considered a comprehensive scientific resource, it demonstrates an appreciation for the animals that inspired the project. This combination of entertainment and educational material gives the experience additional personality.

The game's accessibility is strengthened by its free-to-play availability and relatively modest system requirements. Steam Deck compatibility is officially categorized as Playable rather than fully Verified. Performance with the default graphics configuration is considered suitable, and the game can run successfully on SteamOS. However, handheld players should expect compromises. Some functionality is not fully accessible through the default controller configuration, touchscreen interaction or a community controller layout may occasionally be useful, and text entry can require manually opening the virtual keyboard. Some interface text may also appear small, while certain prompts can display keyboard, mouse, or non-Steam Deck controller icons. It is therefore functional on the Deck, but the experience is less seamless than a fully optimized handheld release.

Ultimately, Dinosaurs A Prehistoric Adventure is a creative but underdeveloped prehistoric action RPG that succeeds more through its unusual ideas than through polished execution. Its selection of playable dinosaurs, fictional environmental catastrophe, survival elements, and educational exhibition provide enough interesting features to justify curiosity, especially considering its free availability. However, repetitive mechanics, basic combat, limited environmental interaction, and modest presentation considerably weaken its lasting appeal. Dinosaur enthusiasts seeking a casual and unconventional experience may discover some entertainment here, while players expecting a sophisticated survival simulator or deeply engaging RPG will likely find it lacking. With stronger gameplay systems and greater technical refinement, its distinctive concept could have supported something considerably more memorable. 

Rating: 5/10
